reviews_5s:
If you're tired of flimsy colanders that wobble, tip, or clog up with water, this is the upgrade you didn’t know you needed. The ExcelSteel Heavy Duty Colander is truly in a class of its own.
From the moment I unboxed it, I could tell it was solid — the stainless steel feels substantial without being overly heavy, and the craftsmanship is excellent. The heavy-duty handles are securely riveted (no fear of them popping off under a load of pasta or veggies), and the self-draining solid ring base is an absolute game-changer. It keeps the colander stable on the sink or counter without tipping or shifting — even when I'm rinsing heavy potatoes or pouring in a full pot of pasta water.
Another huge win: the perforations are perfectly sized and distributed for quick, efficient draining — no standing water at the bottom, no frustration. Plus, the 5-quart capacity is ideal for everything from washing fruits to draining big batches of spaghetti for family dinners.
Bottom line: If you want a colander that’s sturdy, smartly designed, and will probably outlive your kitchen, don’t think twice. This is a must-have tool for any serious (or casual) home cook.

reviews_1s:
Let me just start by saying I have no idea why this colander has such a high rating. A colander has one job, which is to allow water to drain from whatever you place into it. Does this task seem complicated? No. Does this colander transform what should be a simple task into an impossible, near-Sisyphean endeavor? Well, read on to see.

When attempting to use this colander to drain water from some spinach, I found there remained a significant layer of water at the bottom of the colander, try as I might to shake it around to drain the offending liquid. It was as if this colander had suddenly gotten tired of its day job (being a colander) and decided to moonlight as a bowl.

It also feels important to discuss the number of holes that this colander has on its bottom, which is 34. One should not be able to so easily count the number of holes a colander has on the bottom, because it should be a very high number, because that is the point of a colander. It is also essential to point out, as one may be able to note from the picture, that there is significant space between the bottom holes and the side holes, rendering the side holes nothing more than ornamentation, as there is no way that water can or would drain out of them.

To prove just how ineffective this colander is at being a colander, I measured out half a tablespoon of water, poured it into the colander, swished it around, and then poured the remaining water back into the measuring spoon. Reader, I am being completely honest when I tell you that the remaining water nearly filled the measuring spoon all the way up to the top.

Upon deep self-reflection, my plight at having to come to own this sorry excuse for a "colander" may in some ways be what I deserve for purchasing a ten dollar colander from Amazon. I know this review might read as a joke, but the only joke is this colander. I implore you to spend your money elsewhere.There was a massive piece of adhesive tape on the bottom of the colander (like, where you place food) that was taping down nothing at all. After trying everything, including adhesive glue remover spray, the adhesive stickiness remains and renders this product essentially useless to me, since I can’t be putting my food on industrial level sticker glue.This is not a colander, it’s a bowl with a few holes in it. From the entire bottom to 2 inches up the side this thing it is 99% stainless steel, before you once again get to holes up the side where they really aren’t as needed. Once any water is in this “bowl” you have to turn it nearly on its side to get all the remaining water slowly out of it. Do not buyThis colander has literally one job to do: drain water. But it doesn't do that very effectively. There aren't enough holes on the bottom, and so a fair amount of water just sits in there, along with your pasta, grapes, whatever you're straining. It's a really dumb design. I bought this to replace a black plastic colander I've had for 30 years, since I've been reading about the dangers of black plastic - but that one always let all the water drain out. Clearly shiny and new isn't always better.Extremely disappointed. The holes in the strainer are extremely sharp. There was so much gross sticky, and gooey stuff inside on the bottom. I cut my finger trying to get it out.!!! I would never purchase againThis item does not strain well at all.
